sections.subject: Reading
sections.instructions: Read the passage below, then answer questions 1 to 8. Choose the best answer for each question.

passage.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
passage.text:
Mara had lived on Bell Island her whole life, in the small white cottage beside the lighthouse where her father worked. Every evening at dusk, she would climb the spiral stairs with him to watch the great lamp turn on, sending its beam sweeping across the dark water.

"Why does the light have to turn?" Mara asked one evening, as she had asked a hundred times before. She liked hearing her father's answer, even though she already knew it.

"Because a light that never moves is easy to ignore," her father said, polishing the brass railing with a soft cloth. "But a light that sweeps and turns catches the eye of every ship, even ones far out past the reef. It says: here is danger, and here is safety, if you know which way to steer."

That night, a storm rolled in faster than the weather reports had predicted. Mara watched from her window as the wind bent the old pine trees nearly sideways and rain lashed against the glass. She thought of the fishing boats that had left that morning and wondered if they had made it back to the mainland in time.

Around midnight, she heard her father's boots on the stairs, moving quickly. She followed him up to the lamp room, where he was frowning at a control panel covered in small blinking lights. "The automatic timer has failed," he said. "I'll have to turn it by hand until the storm passes, or the light might stop sweeping altogether."

For three hours, Mara sat wrapped in a blanket in the corner of the lamp room while her father turned the great mechanism by a heavy iron crank, over and over, never stopping, his arms shaking with effort by the second hour. She brought him water. She counted his turns to keep him company. When dawn finally broke and the storm eased, a small fishing boat limped into the harbour below, its crew waving up at the lighthouse in thanks.

Later, the boat's captain told anyone who would listen that he'd nearly given up finding the coastline in the storm — until he saw the light, sweeping steady and sure, exactly where it was supposed to be.

questions.text: Where does Mara live?

options.B: In a cottage beside a lighthouse
options.C: In a town on the mainland
options.D: At the top of the lamp room

questions.explanation: The first paragraph states Mara lives 'in the small white cottage beside the lighthouse where her father worked.'

questions.text: According to Mara's father, why does the light need to turn rather than stay still?

options.A: It uses less electricity that way
options.B: A moving light is easier to repair
options.C: A moving light catches the eye more than a still one
options.D: It is a tradition passed down from older lighthouse keepers

questions.explanation: He explains that 'a light that never moves is easy to ignore' but a sweeping light 'catches the eye of every ship.'

questions.text: What problem occurs during the storm?

options.B: A fishing boat crashes near the reef
options.C: The automatic timer that turns the light fails

questions.explanation: The text states 'The automatic timer has failed,' requiring the father to turn the light by hand.

questions.text: What does Mara do while her father operates the light by hand?

options.B: She brings him water and counts his turns
options.C: She tries to fix the timer herself
options.D: She goes to find help from the mainland

questions.explanation: The passage says 'She brought him water. She counted his turns to keep him company.'

questions.text: The phrase 'his arms shaking with effort' suggests that the father is:

options.C: Physically exhausted from the manual work

questions.explanation: Turning a heavy iron crank for hours by hand would cause physical fatigue, shown by his shaking arms.

questions.text: What happens at the end of the story?

options.A: The lighthouse is destroyed by the storm
options.B: A fishing boat safely reaches the harbour, guided by the light
options.D: The automatic timer is fixed before dawn

questions.explanation: 'A small fishing boat limped into the harbour below, its crew waving up at the lighthouse in thanks.'

questions.text: What is the best theme or message of this passage?

options.B: Technology always fails at the worst possible time
options.C: Quiet dedication and hard work can save lives
options.D: Children should not be allowed near dangerous machinery

questions.explanation: The father's tireless manual effort through the night, though unglamorous, directly saves the fishing crew — illustrating dedication and hard work.

questions.text: Which word best describes Mara's role during the storm?
questions.explanation: She stays with her father, brings him water, and counts his turns — a supportive, encouraging presence.

sections.subject: English
sections.instructions: Answer questions 9 to 23. Choose the best answer for each question.

questions.text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.

options.D: It is a beautiful day, outside

questions.explanation: "It's" is the correct contraction of "it is," and the sentence needs a full stop at the end.

questions.text: Which word is a synonym for 'enormous'?
questions.explanation: "Massive" means very large, the same as "enormous."

questions.text: Identify the adjective in this sentence: 'The curious cat explored the quiet garden.'
questions.explanation: "Curious" describes the cat, making it the adjective (though "quiet" also qualifies, "curious" is the first and clearest answer here).

questions.text: Which sentence uses the correct plural form?
questions.explanation: "Children" is the correct irregular plural of "child."

questions.text: What is the antonym of 'ancient'?
questions.explanation: "Modern" is the opposite of "ancient."

questions.text: Choose the sentence written in the past tense.

options.B: She will run to the shop.
options.D: She is running to the shop.

questions.explanation: "Ran" is the past tense of "run."

questions.text: Which word correctly completes the sentence: 'Neither the dog nor the cats ___ hungry.'
questions.explanation: With "neither/nor," the verb agrees with the noun closest to it — "cats" is plural, so "are" is correct.

questions.text: Identify the compound word.
questions.explanation: "Basketball" combines "basket" and "ball" into one word.

questions.text: Which sentence contains a simile?

options.A: The moon was a silver coin.
options.B: Her smile was as bright as the sun.
options.C: The wind whispered through the trees.

questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using "like" or "as" — "as bright as the sun" is a simile.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.explanation: "Receive" follows the rule "i before e except after c" correctly.

questions.text: What type of sentence is this: 'Please close the door.'
questions.explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command or request, like "Please close the door."

questions.text: Which word is a preposition in this sentence: 'The book is under the table.'
questions.explanation: "Under" shows the relationship between the book and the table, making it a preposition.

questions.text: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement.

options.A: The team are winning the game.
options.B: The team is winning the game.
options.C: The team were winning the game (present tense).
options.D: The team be winning the game.

questions.explanation: "Team" is treated as a singular collective noun here, so it takes "is."

questions.text: What does the prefix 'un-' mean in the word 'unhappy'?
questions.explanation: The prefix "un-" means "not," so "unhappy" means "not happy."

questions.text: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

options.A: Me and him went to the park.
options.B: Him and me went to the park.
options.C: He and I went to the park.

questions.explanation: "He and I" is the correct subject pronoun form for the sentence's subject.

sections.subject: Mathematics
sections.instructions: Answer questions 24 to 43. No calculator is permitted. Choose the best answer for each question.

questions.text: What is 6 × 7 × 2?
What is 144 ÷ 12?
What fraction of this shape is shaded if 3 out of 8 equal parts are shaded?
questions.explanation: 3 shaded parts out of 8 total parts is written as 3/8.

questions.text: What is 0.6 written as a fraction in simplest form?
questions.explanation: 0.6 = 6/10, which simplifies to 3/5.

questions.text: A recipe needs 250g of flour to make 5 muffins. How much flour is needed for 20 muffins?
questions.explanation: 20 muffins is 4 times 5 muffins, so 250g × 4 = 1000g.

questions.text: What is the perimeter of a rectangle with length 12cm and width 7cm?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width) = 2 × (12 + 7) = 2 × 19 = 38cm.

questions.text: What is the area of a square with sides of 9cm?
questions.explanation: Area of a square = side × side = 9 × 9 = 81cm².

questions.text: Round 4,682 to the nearest hundred.
questions.explanation: 4,682 is closer to 4,700 than 4,600, since the tens digit (8) rounds up.

questions.text: What is 25% of 160?
questions.explanation: 25% is one quarter, and 160 ÷ 4 = 40.

questions.text: If a train travels at 60km/h, how far does it travel in 2.5 hours?
questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150km.

questions.text: What is the next number in the pattern: 3, 9, 27, 81, ___?
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 3: 81 × 3 = 243.

questions.text: What is the value of the digit 7 in the number 47,283?
questions.explanation: The 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7,000.

questions.text: A triangle has angles of 55° and 65°. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle add to 180°. 180 − 55 − 65 = 60°.

questions.text: What is 5⁄6 − 1⁄3?
How many millilitres are in 2.5 litres?
questions.explanation: 1 litre = 1,000mL, so 2.5 litres = 2,500mL.

questions.text: A shop sells pencils in packs of 8. If Tom buys 60 pencils, how many packs did he buy, and how many pencils are left over?
questions.explanation: 60 ÷ 8 = 7 remainder 4, so 7 full packs with 4 pencils left over.

questions.text: What is the mean (average) of 4, 8, 6, 10, 12?
Which number sentence is true?
questions.explanation: 3/4 = 0.75 and 2/3 ≈ 0.667, so 3/4 is greater than 2/3.

sections.subject: General Ability
sections.instructions: Answer questions 44 to 58. Choose the best answer for each question.

questions.text: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Apple, Banana and Orange are fruits; Carrot is a vegetable.

questions.text: Complete the analogy: Bird is to Nest as Bee is to ___
questions.explanation: A bird lives in a nest, just as a bee lives in a hive.

questions.text: What comes next in the pattern: 2, 4, 8, 16, ___?
questions.explanation: Each number doubles the previous one: 16 × 2 = 32.

questions.text: If all Zibs are Wozzles, and all Wozzles are Blue, which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: If Zibs are a subset of Wozzles, and Wozzles are all Blue, then Zibs must also all be Blue.

questions.text: Which shape completes the pattern: Square, Circle, Triangle, Square, Circle, ___?
questions.explanation: The pattern repeats every 3 shapes: Square, Circle, Triangle. The next one is Triangle.

questions.text: Sam is taller than Jess. Jess is taller than Mia. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: Sam > Jess > Mia in height, so Mia is the shortest.

questions.text: Which word means the opposite of 'expand'?
questions.explanation: "Contract" means to become smaller, the opposite of "expand."

questions.text: Complete the analogy: Author is to Book as Composer is to ___
questions.explanation: An author creates a book, just as a composer creates music.

questions.text: What is the missing number: 5, 10, 20, 40, ___, 160?
questions.explanation: Each number doubles: 40 × 2 = 80, and 80 × 2 = 160, confirming the pattern.

questions.text: Three friends, Ali, Ben and Cara, are sitting in a row. Ali is not sitting next to Cara. Ben is in the middle. Who is sitting where?

options.C: Both A and B are possible

questions.explanation: With Ben in the middle, Ali and Cara are on either side, meaning they are not next to each other in either arrangement.

questions.text: Which number does not belong: 4, 9, 16, 20, 25?
questions.explanation: 4, 9, 16 and 25 are all perfect squares (2², 3², 4², 5²); 20 is not.

questions.text: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be in 10 days?
questions.explanation: 10 days from Wednesday: 7 days brings you back to Wednesday, plus 3 more days = Saturday.

questions.text: Which word is spelled correctly and means 'to make something better'?
questions.explanation: "Improve" is the correct spelling and means to make something better.

questions.text: If MOUSE is coded as NPVTF (each letter shifted forward by 1 in the alphabet), how is CAT coded using the same rule?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts forward by one: C→D, A→B, T→U, giving DBU.

questions.text:
Which figure is the odd one out?
(Imagine 4 shapes: three are shaded triangles pointing up, one is a shaded triangle pointing down.)
questions.explanation: Three triangles point the same direction (up); the odd one out points down.
